clue.text: Loose cover cushions, elastic edges

indicators.note: a cushion surrounds and pads what it holds, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: to insure something is to give it cover against loss

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A sofa cover has gone slack because the elastic around the cushions has worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cushions' looks like a noun but is the verb: INSURE cushions EC, the edges of 'elastic'.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose fastening is not firmly fixed, which is one sense of insecure.

clue.text: As Eddie Izzard might appear after daring transformation?

indicators.note: a transformation changes a thing's form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: How the comedian Eddie Izzard looks after a bold change of image.
explanation.walkthrough: Eddie Izzard is a British comedian known for performing in women's clothes and make-up.
explanation.definitionFit: In drag means dressed in clothing usually worn by another gender, as Izzard often performs.

clue.text: It chops up fresh apple

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to chop is to axe, so chops gives axes

indicators.note: fresh means new, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Something that slices a fresh apple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' looks like the chopping tool, but it is the definition: 'it' was once slang for sexual magnetism, as in the It girl.
explanation.definitionFit: 'It' is old slang for magnetic allure, the quality that made Clara Bow the It girl.

clue.text: "Flawless Salah toying with Newcastle" — Independent claimed

indicators.note: toying with something is playing around with it, so the letters are mixed
claimed means taken in, so the I is added to the mix

explanation.surface: A newspaper headline: Mo Salah was flawless in toying with Newcastle, the Independent said.
explanation.walkthrough: Mohamed Salah is the Liverpool forward; Newcastle United are a Premier League football club, here the anagram's fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Clean as a whistle is an idiom for spotless, without any fault or stain.

clue.text: A good daughter filling bap for her playmate?

indicators.note: a filling goes inside, like the filling of a sandwich

parts.note: a bap is a soft bread roll

explanation.surface: A good daughter makes a sandwich roll for her friend to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: A bap is a British soft bread roll. 'her playmate?' is a definition by example, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A rag doll is a soft cloth toy, the sort a little girl might have as a companion.

clue.text: I had contracted cold when accepting Oscar for Dumb & Dumber feature

parts.note: I had shortened to its contraction is I'd

indicators.note: a word accepting another takes it inside itself

parts.note: icy means very cold
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone with a cold, who has won an Oscar, picks out a trait of the film Dumb and Dumber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when accepting' signals the insertion of the Oscar letter. Dumb and Dumber is a 1994 comedy about two very stupid friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Stupidity is the chief trait of that film's heroes, and idiocy names that foolishness.

clue.text: Vital I'd had gonad treated; in this case a sling helped

definitions.text: in this case a sling helped

indicators.note: treating something works on it and changes it, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A patient had an important gland treated, and wore a sling afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sling' looks medical, but it is David's sling, the weapon he used to kill the giant Goliath.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible story young David defeats the giant Goliath with a stone from his sling.

clue.text: Senior citizen trapped in café I'd locked up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top
letters trapped in other words lie within them

explanation.surface: A pensioner shut inside a café that I had locked.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs backwards across cafE I'D LOcked: 'trapped in' hides it and 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: An oldie is an informal word for an old person, a pensioner.

clue.text: Golly Sue! Amazing cakes!

indicators.note: something amazing is bewildering, so the letters are thrown into confusion

explanation.surface: An exclamation of delight at some wonderful cakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Yule logs are chocolate sponge rolls decorated to look like logs at Christmas.

clue.text: Geek turned on taps to make things wet

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so the first piece comes first
turned means read the other way round

parts.note: a geek is a nerd
taps are marked C and H, for cold and hot

explanation.surface: A nerd switches on the taps and soaks everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned on' looks like one phrase for switching on, but 'turned' reverses NERD and 'on' puts it above CH.
explanation.definitionFit: To drench is to soak something thoroughly with water.

clue.text: 9 or 11 perish touring Southern states

indicators.note: touring means going round, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: to perish is to die
9 is IX and 11 is XI in Roman numerals; either works

explanation.surface: Something about the number 9 or 11 dying out on a tour of the American South.
explanation.walkthrough: '9 or 11' is fair because either Roman numeral, placed by 'touring' at its own spot, yields the same five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Dixie is the nickname for the southern US states of the old Confederacy.

clue.text: US writer, associate of Clinton (Bill), pens 6D

indicators.note: to pen something is to enclose it, as in a pen, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Bill Clinton's vice-president was Al Gore, written surname first as Gore, Al to match the style 'Clinton (Bill)'
6 is VI in Roman numerals, followed by the D

explanation.surface: An American author linked to Bill Clinton writes something referring to another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: '6D' looks like a cross-reference to 6 Down but is read literally as Roman six plus D. 'Clinton (Bill)' sets the surname-first style, so the vice-president is written that way too.
explanation.definitionFit: Gore Vidal was an American novelist and essayist, author of Myra Breckinridge.

clue.text: Starts to help out navy following plane crash — it's blown up

indicators.note: the second part comes after the first in the answer
a plane crash leaves the word's letters in a jumbled heap
the starts of words are their first letters

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A rescue appeal: help is needed from the navy after a plane has crashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crash' scrambles the aircraft word and 'following' sets the rest after it. The definition plays on 'up' as up in the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: An alpenhorn is a long wooden horn blown by herdsmen high in the Alps.

clue.text: Live with depression having taken over

indicators.note: taking a letter over means taking charge of it, holding it within

parts.note: a dell is a small hollow or valley

explanation.surface: Advice about living with depression after it has taken control of a life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depression' reads as low mood, but here it is a dip in the land; 'having taken over' puts W inside DELL.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell somewhere is to reside or make a home there.

clue.text: Wee man steals regularly, treacherous character

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every other one

explanation.surface: A small man who habitually steals is a sly, untrustworthy sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the first, third, fifth letters and so on across WEEMANSTEALS.
explanation.definitionFit: A weasel is a sneaky, untrustworthy person, from the animal's crafty reputation.

clue.text: According to Spooner, blacklisted crone Thatcher carried one

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of two words trade places

parts.note: something blacklisted is banned
a hag is an ugly old woman

explanation.surface: An insult to Margaret Thatcher as a shunned old crone.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of BANNED HAG to get HAND BAG. Margaret Thatcher, British prime minister 1979-90, was famous for her handbag.
explanation.definitionFit: Her ever-present handbag became a symbol of Thatcher's style, even giving rise to the verb to handbag.

clue.text: British upper-class tea break? Capital!

parts.note: U denotes upper-class usage in British English
cha is British slang for tea
a rest is a break

explanation.surface: A posh British tea break, greeted with the old exclamation 'Capital!'
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital!' looks like a dated British cry of approval but is the definition: a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Bucharest is the capital city of Romania.

clue.text: Cancelled actor Johnny bends over

indicators.note: turned over means reversed

parts.note: Johnny Depp is the American actor
arcs are bends or curves

explanation.surface: A cancelled actor, Johnny Depp, gives in to pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses DEPP ARCS as a whole. The surface plays on Depp's well-publicised fall from favour.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scrapped has been abandoned or called off.

clue.text: Frosty relations put elderly wife on board coach

indicators.note: putting something on board a vehicle puts it inside

parts.note: a coach is a railway carriage, also called a car
elderly means old

explanation.surface: Relations are cool after an old wife is put on the coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coach' suggests a bus, but here it is a railway carriage; 'on board' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cold War was the long period of tension, short of fighting, between the US and the Soviet bloc.

clue.text: Do some research about American political party

parts.note: re means about or concerning
the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Someone investigating an American political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American political party' looks like one phrase, but A is American and the party is the DUP, from Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: To read up on a topic is to study it thoroughly.

clue.text: Following death, it's transferred on account last thing on Friday

parts.note: in cricket the leg side is also called the on side

indicators.note: the last thing in a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A bank transfer made into an account at the end of Friday after someone has died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' becomes LEG through cricket, where the leg side of the pitch is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: A legacy is money or property left in a will and passed on after its owner dies.

clue.text: Play large English bloke at wedding

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
the groom is the man getting married

explanation.surface: A cast list: a play with a big English chap at a wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' looks like a drama, but it means room to move, as in play in a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Legroom is space to stretch one's legs, and play means freedom of movement.

clue.text: Frenzied husband on ecstasy with constant twitch

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
c is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A husband high on ecstasy keeps twitching wildly.
explanation.definitionFit: Hectic describes a period full of frantic, rushed activity.

clue.text: The greatest Belgium international defence

parts.note: Muhammad Ali called himself The Greatest
B is the international vehicle code for Belgium

explanation.surface: The finest Belgian international footballer is a defender.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a defence claiming the accused was somewhere else at the time.

clue.text: Skerry not available for rent?

definitions.meaning: a skerry is a small rocky island
read as two words, ...: a place that ... is already rented out, so not available

explanation.surface: A tiny rocky island that no one can rent.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the answer as two words, IS LET; the question mark flags the split.
explanation.definitionFit: A skerry is a reef or tiny rocky island, and an islet is a small island.

clue.text: Merkel, say, by Karlsruhe on vacation receiving cold sponge

indicators.note: by means next to, so the pieces sit side by side
receiving means taking something in

parts.note: Angela Merkel, former German chancellor, is an example of an Angela
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: a word on vacation is emptied, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: Angela Merkel, at Karlsruhe, is given a cold sponge, as if at a spa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' empties Karlsruhe to KE; 'receiving' then puts C inside ANGELAKE.
explanation.definitionFit: Angel cake is a light, airy sponge made with whisked egg whites.

clue.text: Endlessly refined massage turned on nameless Soviet leaders

indicators.note: without its end, the last letter is cut off

parts.note: refined manners are polite

indicators.note: turned round means read backwards

parts.note: to massage is to rub

indicators.note: N is the abbreviation for name, so nameless means without an N

parts.note: taken as the word itself before cutting

explanation.surface: A refined massage given to nameless Soviet leaders, as if at a Kremlin spa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' cuts POLITE to POLIT, 'turned' makes RUB into BUR, and 'nameless' takes N from ON, leaving O.
explanation.definitionFit: The Politburo was the chief policy-making committee of the Soviet Communist Party.

clue.text: Skilful head of Art Department

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A clever leader of a university art department.
explanation.definitionFit: Adept describes someone highly competent and expert.

clue.text: Hesitate to visit Rawalpindi therapist

indicators.note: a word visiting others is staying in them, so the answer lies within these letters

explanation.surface: Someone wavers over seeing a therapist in Rawalpindi.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the gap in RawalpinDI THERapist. Rawalpindi is a city in Pakistan.
explanation.definitionFit: To dither is to be unable to make up one's mind.

clue.text: Eminem's debut at microphone "arresting, terrific, forceful"

indicators.note: a debut is a first appearance, so the word's first letter
arresting means catching and holding, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: mic is short for microphone
phat is hip-hop slang for excellent

explanation.surface: A review of Eminem's first time at the mic: striking, superb, powerful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arresting' looks like praise but signals the insertion; 'terrific' is hip-hop slang, which suits the rapper's world.
explanation.definitionFit: An emphatic statement is made with force and conviction.
